messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English in close third person from one adult character's point of view. Keep the narration anchored to what that character can directly notice, remember, infer, or feel. Do not jump into the other character's private thoughts. Use natural dialogue and selective description.

Alex knew Jordan was upset before Jordan said anything.

It was the silence.

Jordan usually complained about traffic before she even took off her coat. Today she came inside, hung it neatly, and went straight to the kitchen.

Alex followed.

“You want coffee?”

Jordan opened the cabinet. “No.”

Alex stopped in the doorway.

That answer felt wrong.

“Tea?”

“No.”

“Water?”

Jordan looked over.

“I'm fine.”

Alex didn't believe her, but she didn't know why.

She watched Jordan take a glass from the shelf and fill it from the sink.

“You sure?”

“Yeah.”

Jordan drank half the glass in one go.

Alex leaned against the counter.

She could ask what happened. She could push. She could wait.

Waiting usually worked better with Jordan.

Alex opened the refrigerator.

“There's leftover pasta.”

Jordan nodded.

“Okay.”

Alex pulled out the container and set it on the counter.

Jordan looked at it, then gave a tired little smile.

“Thanks.”

“Sure.”

Alex put the container in the microwave.

While it turned, Jordan stood beside the counter and stared at nothing in particular.

Alex didn't try to guess what she was thinking.

She just stayed there.
